question: What is the diameter size range of the virus?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Viruses**:-

 
 
• These are incredibly tiny, infectious particles that can only reproduce inside living cells.
 
• They are much smaller than bacteria and can only be seen with an electron microscope. 
 
• **Viruses **are made up of **genetic material (DNA or RNA)** enclosed in a protein coat called a **capsid**.
 
• Some viruses also have an envelope, which is a layer of fat and protein that surrounds the capsid. The genetic material inside the virus contains the instructions for making new viruses. 
 
• The diameter size range of viruses varies greatly, from about **20 nanometers (nm) to 500 nm**.
 
• For comparison, a human hair is about 100,000 nm wide.
